components.name: Primary Black Pill
components.description: High-contrast primary action pill across landing CTAs, Login, and Quick AI Diagnosis.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: #000000; color: #FFFFFF; font-weight: 600; font-size: 13.5px; border: none; border-radius: 999px; padding: 10px 22px; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.15s, transform 0.15s; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #262626; transform: scale(1.025); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #1B98F2; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Rainbow AI Pipeline Pill
components.description: Horizon-bordered pill reserved exclusively for the 6-Agent Investigation trigger.
components.css: .ds-btn-rainbow { background: linear-gradient(#FFFFFF, #FFFFFF) padding-box, linear-gradient(225deg, #1B98F2, #CF69E0, #F56293, #FF635C, #FF8C51) border-box; color: #000000; font-weight: 700; font-size: 13.5px; border: 2px solid transparent; border-radius: 999px; padding: 10px 22px; cursor: pointer; transition: box-shadow 0.2s, transform 0.15s; } .ds-btn-rainbow:hover { box-shadow: 0 4px 16px rgba(207, 105, 224, 0.28); transform: scale(1.025); }

components.name: Secondary Frost Pill

narrative.overview:
IncidentIQ translates the high-contrast light editorial calm of https://www.serko.ai/ into a native JavaFX 21 desktop workbench backed by Spring Boot telemetry. Rather than immersing engineers in noisy dark-mode neon panels, the interface treats production incident triage like an architectural press sheet: pure white surfaces framed by soft frost cards, disciplined pure-black typography, and a focused horizon spectrum reserved exclusively for AI intelligence and primary hero breakthroughs.

Every flow—from the animated 3D wireframe telemetry globe on the public Home showcase through JWT authentication into the split-pane Incident Queue, Report ingestion, and Operational Analytics—inherits the exact same spatial cadence, pill geometry, and restrained signal palette.
keyCharacteristics: Pure white canvases paired with soft frost surfaces and ice-sky feature bands rather than saturated backgrounds or dark mode.
Multi-stop sky-to-sunset spectrum (horizon-blue through horizon-purple, horizon-pink, and aura-ember) reserved for AI agent triggers, hero horizon atmosphere, and headline emphasis.
Universal 999px capsule pill affordances for actions, navigation switchers, and semantic status badges.
Selective HTML5 Canvas (WebView) integration inside native JavaFX scenes strictly where real-time 3D geodesic projection outperforms static vectors.

rules.name: The Horizon Restraint Rule
rules.body: Full multi-stop gradients belong exclusively to hero/CTA horizon backdrops, inline headline emphasis words, progress bars, and the tertiary 6-Agent Investigation pill border—never fill standard workspace cards or tables with saturated gradients.

rules.name: The Mnemonic Guard Rule
rules.body: Disable JavaFX mnemonic parsing on every dynamic or underscore-containing chip (APPLICATION_BUG, MEMORY_LEAK) so underscores render verbatim instead of being eaten as Alt-key accelerators.

rules.name: The Flat-Track Rule
rules.body: Segmented pill tracks and filter strips never cast drop shadows; only the selected active pill floats inside its frost track.

dos: Do preserve 100% light editorial grounds (#FFFFFF / #F6F6F6 / #E8F3FE) and pure black typography (#000000) across every route.
Do use native JavaFX SVGPath icons (brandLogoMark, chevronRightIcon, vector bolts) so glyphs render identically across Windows DPI configurations.
Do render multi-agent and quick AI outputs as scannable structured cards rather than unbroken walls of monospace log dumps.

Do set setMinWidth(Region.USE_PREF_SIZE) (leaving prefWidth at USE_COMPUTED_SIZE inside an unconstrained Pane host) on horizontal marquee labels and status pills inside flex HBox rows so labels never ellipsis-truncate or collapse to zero width.
donts: Don't introduce dark-mode surfaces (#0d0d1a, neon cyan cards) anywhere in the inside workspace or auth screens (the public footer #000000 is the sole deliberate dark anchor).
Don't use CSS degree angles (linear-gradient(155deg, ...)) inside JavaFX stylesheets or inline styles; JavaFX CSS strictly requires directional keywords (to bottom right) or percentage coordinates.

Don't pass opaque/translucent backdrops (rgba(255,255,255,0.92)) onto sticky scrolled toolbars in JavaFX where backdrop-filter: blur is unsupported—use solid #FFFFFF once scrolled so scrolling headlines do not bleed faintly underneath nav links.
